known_limitations: No tests were executed; this is static test authorship only, per policy (no Unity/build/test execution performed).

The new test uses an in-memory Image component with a manually assigned color to simulate the scene's blue-tinted fill Image; it does not open the committed DoorPrototype.unity scene to read the actual authored m_Color value, since committed-scene conformance testing was outside this task's file-write scope.
PlayerManaUI.cs and PlayerMana.cs are read-only to this role; the code already reflects the fix the prior validator pass required, but that was not verified by re-running any suite.

Human Play Mode / visual verification of the actual blue mana-fill indicator flashing and reverting correctly in the real DoorPrototype scene is still required, since no automated test opens or inspects that committed scene's Image color.
structured_output.proposed_unity_test_scope: Play Mode behavior tests (UnityTest coroutines) plus one pure/component reflection-based test, all using freshly constructed in-memory GameObjects (PlayerMana, PlayerManaUI, Image) rather than the committed DoorPrototype.unity scene. Suite: NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests / PlayerManaPlayModeTests via Unity Test Runner (Play Mode), filter class=NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.PlayerManaPlayModeTests. No scene, prefab, or ScriptableObject asset is opened or saved; non-mutation invariant is preserved by construction (all objects are created and destroyed within each test's SetUp/TearDown or try/finally block).
structured_output.summary: The existing PlayerManaPlayModeTests.cs already covered AC-001 (ResetMana), AC-002 (CastDenied event + UI flash), AC-003 (public API surface lock), and VAL-002/VAL-003 (readable low-mana feedback). Production PlayerManaUI.cs in the working tree already contains the previously-flagged fix (capturing the fill Image's actual color in OnEnable instead of a hardcoded white default). I added one new regression test, PlayerManaUI_RevertsToActualFillImageColor_NotHardcodedDefault, that sets the Image's color to a non-default blue (simulating the scene's actual m_Color) before enabling PlayerManaUI, then asserts the denied-flash correctly reverts to that captured blue rather than a hardcoded default. This closes the gap the validator identified: prior tests only used AddComponent<Image>()'s default white color, which coincidentally matched the hardcoded field-initializer default and could not distinguish a real fix from the original bug. No production code was modified.
